newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak signs $100 mln subordinated debt.
newsitem.headline: Slovak signs $100 mln subordinated debt.

text.p: Slovakia's largest commercial bank, VUB a.s., on Thursday said it had signed a $100 million, 10-year subordinated debt issue with U.S.-based investment bank Merill Lynch.

"We (VUB) have already drawn funds from the issue, and with the managing bank we will hold a roadshow in London at the end of January to sell the bonds further," Jozef Galis, Director of VUB's Foreign Exchange Relations Department, told Reuters.
Galis added taht the fiduciary bank Bankers Trust Luxemberg had already issued the debt bonds, with the entire tranche taken by Merill Lynch.
He declined to comment on the price of the issue and said it was now up to Meryll Lynch to decide what volume it will keep and what amount will be distributed further.
"The destination (for the bonds) will be Hong Kong and South Korea," Galis said.
He said that the bonds are callable after five years, but added this would require approval of the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS).
Galis said the bank did not meet the capital adequacy ratio required by the NBS before the move, but added that after the issue the ratio stood at the demanded 8.0 percent.
Moody's Investors Service rating for VUB is Ba1 for long- term deposits, not prime for short-term deposits and D for financial strength.

VUB is among the four largest Slovak financial institutions, including the savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna, commercial bank IRB and insurer Slovenska Poistovna, which are still effectively controled by the state through stakes held by the privatisation agency, the National Property Fund.
The privatisation of the four has been postoned by law until March 31.

Merrill Lynch has also managed a $80 million tranche of subordinated debt for VUB's rival Slovenska Sporitelna at the end of last year. Sporitelna's debt bonds carried an interest rate of LIBOR plus 125 basis points in the fist five years, with the remaining five years at LIBOR plus 300 basis points.
